title: The Fathers, again
hookLine: the glory of God is a person fully alive
tomorrow: the first Christians hit a huge fight. how did they settle it?

cards: Graduation cards love it. So do coffee mugs and gym walls: the glory of God is a person fully alive. It's credited to Irenaeus, a bishop of Lyons and one of the early Church Fathers.
Here's the thing. He didn't quite say it like that. In his Latin it reads gloria Dei vivens homo: the glory of God is a living human being.
And the sentence doesn't stop there.

teach.b: The rest of it: and the life of a human being is the vision of God. So the poster version keeps half. Irenaeus isn't cheering for living your best life in general.
He's saying two things at once. God's glory and human flourishing aren't rivals; a living, breathing person is what God's glory looks like.
And what makes a person truly alive is seeing God, turning toward the one who made them.

That's the Fathers in a nutshell: the early teachers, bishops and writers whose words the Church still reads, holding faith and real life in one hand. Another of them, Augustine, puts the same thing as a longing.

teach.h: RESTLESS UNTIL IT REPOSE IN THEE.
teach.b: In Pusey's old translation of his Confessions: "for Thou madest us for Thyself, and our heart is restless, until it repose in Thee."
So for a week like this one, a big choice, a scary yes, a plan that thrills you and terrifies you, the Fathers don't say want less.
They say want rightly. Something to tell a friend tonight: the line on the mug is a loose rendering, and the real sentence is bigger. Alive, and seeing God.

how: Catholics hear the Church Fathers in the Office of Readings of the Liturgy of the Hours, where a passage from an early teacher is read nearly every day alongside scripture.

s: Irenaeus wrote 'the glory of God is a person fully alive'
that's a loose rendering; he wrote a living human being, whose life is the vision of God.
Augustine wrote that our heart is restless until it rests in God
near the opening of his Confessions.
the Church Fathers were the first popes
they're early teachers and writers, bishops like Irenaeus and Augustine among them.

games.q: your friend thinks being religious means shrinking: no ambition, no joy, just rules. what would Irenaeus say?
o: God's glory is a living person, whose life is seeing God.
she's right: holiness means wanting less of everything.
joy is fine, but it has nothing at all to do with God.
games.why: for Irenaeus, God's glory and human life aren't rivals: a living person is God's glory, and seeing God is that person's life.

practice: Take something to eat or drink, even a sip of water, and give it your whole attention: the temperature, the taste, the swallow. Being fully alive can start this small, present to one gift.
At the end, anyone who prays can give thanks for it.
